newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Truck shortages reported.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Truck shortages reported.

text.p: Truck shortages were forcing country elevators to dump thousands of bushels of newly harvested hard red winter wheat on the ground, grain dealers said Wednesday.
"We've got a lot of elevators that have gone on the ground with their grain. There's just no trucks out there to use," a north central Oklahoma dealer said.

Dealers said truck shortages were common around harvest time, but that this year's problem was severe because harvesting was proceeding at the same time in the three big HRW wheat growing states of Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas.
Dealers pinned the problem in part on rains that delayed harvesting for several weeks in Texas. By the time the rains stopped, harvesting was also under way north of Texas.
But another dealer complained that the grain industry was also to blame.

"Over the last three to four years we've pressured rates so cheap that we've put a lot of truckers out of business," another Oklahoma dealer said. "Now we've got a bumper crop and we're paying the price."
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
